title: Fix Process GPU showing no tracked processes
description:

Fix: Verify process_gpu data flows from SystemMetricsCollector through aggregator.py to the frontend.

title: Fix Session Energy showing 0 while Today's Energy increases
description:
Session Energy shows 0 but Today's Energy at the top of the page increases correctly. Session Energy is a separate metric that should track energy usage for the current session. The cost_data is extracted from database but may not include session_energy.

Fix: Investigate where Session Energy should come from and ensure it's properly calculated and displayed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix CPU Power showing 0 - cpu_power_w not extracted in aggregator
description:
The CPU Power metric shows 0 because the aggregator's collect_all_metrics() doesn't properly extract cpu_power_w from system metrics. The SystemMetricsCollector should provide this data but aggregator.py's system_data extraction may be missing this field.

Fix: Verify cpu_power_w flows from SystemMetricsCollector through aggregator.py to the frontend.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix Requests Processing showing 0 - missing from aggregator metrics
description:
The Requests Processing metric shows 0 because the aggregator's collect_all_metrics() doesn't properly extract the requests_processing value from server metrics. The ServerMetricsCollector returns this in the server object but aggregator.py extracts it to server_data which is returned as server in the result. The aggregator_daemon properly extracts this but aggregator.py may have a different data flow.

Investigate and fix to ensure requests_processing flows through to the frontend.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix Active Slots showing 0/0 - slots data not included in aggregator metrics
description:
The aggregator's collect_all_metrics() method returns server_metrics from ServerMetricsCollector but doesn't include the slots array. The frontend expects server.slots to be an array of slot objects to calculate active slots and progress. The ServerMetricsCollector.collect() returns {timestamp, server, slots, props} but aggregator only extracts the 'server' portion and discards 'slots' and 'props'.

Fix: Update aggregator.py's collect_all_metrics() to include slots and props in the returned metrics dictionary.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix Slot Progress & Context card layout and label overlap
description:
## Why

The Slot Progress and Context Used card has multiple layout issues:

1. **Card stretches vertically** - The charts expand to fill available space instead of having consistent margins like other cards
2. **Label overlap at 0%** - The percentage value label (e.g., '0%') overlaps the 'Slot #' text on the left side of the chart
3. **No maximum height** - With many slots, the chart grows to bloated proportions instead of capping at a reasonable height

## What Needs To Be Done

- Fix the card to fill available space with consistent margins between cards
- Prevent visual elements from overlapping, especially the percentage value label at 0% covering 'Slot #' text
- Implement a maximum height for graph elements that caps the chart height
- When there are too many elements to fit at max font size, allow text to shrink
- OR alternatively grow the card if necessary

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Card fills available space with consistent margins between cards (same margins as other cards)
2. Visual elements do not overlap - including percentage value when at 0% (should not cover 'Slot #' text)
3. Graph elements have a maximum height - they don't expand to bloated proportions
4. Text labels have a maximum font size matching other cards for consistency
5. If too many elements to fit at max size, text is allowed to shrink

title: Tokens/Sec graph Y-axes should track session maximum (like CPU/GPU 0-100 scale)
description:
## Why

The Tokens/Sec graph currently auto-scales its y-axes based on recent data, causing constant visual noise as the graph resizes while data scrolls by. The user wants it to behave like the CPU/GPU usage graph which always shows 0-100.

## Requirements

- Both y-axes (left for Processed, right for Generated) should track the maximum value seen during the session
- The maximum should persist for the full runtime (not between sessions)
- The minimum should always be 0 for both axes
- The scale should only increase when a new maximum is seen, never decrease
- This eliminates visual noise from constant rescaling while still adapting to higher speeds

## Implementation Notes

- Track session_max_tokens_processed and session_max_tokens_generated in JavaScript
- When updating the chart, set y.min = 0 and y.max = session_max (or the existing max if higher)
- Update session_max when new data exceeds it
- The CPU/GPU chart already does this with min: 0, max: 100 - use that as a model

title: Reset Tokens/Sec graph to 0 when idle
description:
Tokens/Sec graph stays at 23 t/s and 450 t/s when system is idle (no requests processing).

## Expected Behavior

- When no tokens are being generated: Tokens Generated/s should be 0
- When no tokens are being processed: Tokens Processed/s should be 0
- The graph should accurately reflect that values have stopped changing (rate = 0)

## Important: Do NOT Clear History

- Keep all historical data points
- Just ensure the current/last value accurately shows 0 when idle
- The issue is likely in how the current value is calculated or displayed, not in history retention

## Root Cause to Investigate

- Is the server sending 0 for `predicted_tokens_seconds` and `prompt_tokens_seconds` when idle?
- Is the frontend caching/storing old values instead of updating with new ones?
- Is there a calculation issue (e.g., rate calculation vs absolute value)?
notes:
Check frontend processing first to see if code is deliberately hiding 0 values.

## Investigation Plan

1. Check if server is sending 0 for predicted_tokens_seconds and prompt_tokens_seconds when idle
2. Check if frontend is doing any transformation that might hide 0 values
3. If frontend is hiding 0 intentionally (e.g., to show previous value), this needs to be fixed

title: Fix Llama Monitor webpage showing 0s - architecture mismatch between aggregator and web server
description:
## Problem

The Llama Monitor webpage shows all 0s and 'No tracked processes found' on Windows. The original architecture was:

1. main.py starts aggregator and web server
2. Aggregator gets data from Nvidia, Windows performance counters, etc.
3. Aggregator serves data on port 8081
4. Web server reads data from port 8081
5. Web server shows user GUI with that data

A subagent changed this to use shared memory (metrics_cache) between aggregator and web server threads, but:
- The frontend JavaScript still fetches from http://localhost:8081/api/metrics/latest (aggregator daemon port)
- When running via main.py, no aggregator daemon runs on port 8081
- The aggregator runs as a thread sharing metrics_cache with the web server
- The web server's /api/metrics/latest endpoint checks metrics_cache first, but frontend isn't calling it

## Current State

The frontend JavaScript in web_server.py (lines 979-1004) fetches from port 8081:


When running via main.py:
- Aggregator runs as a thread (not a daemon) on port 8081
- No HTTP API exists on port 8081
- metrics_cache is shared between aggregator thread and web server thread
- Web server's /api/metrics/latest checks metrics_cache first, but frontend doesn't call it

## Possible Fixes

1. Fix main.py to properly connect aggregator and web server via shared memory
2. Investigate whether metrics_cache is implemented correctly for sharing data
3. Investigate what data is being shared over metrics_cache
4. Reimplement the web API from the aggregator daemon on port 8081
5. Even if we get shared memory working, reimplement the web API anyway as a fallback

## Files to Investigate

- main.py - how aggregator and web server are started
- web_server.py - metrics_cache usage and /api/metrics/latest endpoint
- aggregator.py - how metrics_cache is populated
- aggregator_daemon.py - original HTTP API implementation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Webpage displays actual values from today's energy tracking
- Frontend correctly fetches data from the aggregator (either via shared memory or HTTP API)
- Config settings are properly used (web.aggregator_port)
close_reason: The fix is complete. The architecture now correctly uses metrics_cache shared between aggregator and web server threads. The web server's /api/metrics/latest endpoint checks metrics_cache first, and the frontend fetches from this endpoint. All 154 tests pass.

title: Discuss git/worktree cleanup policies to prevent lost work
description:
We have a process issue where worktrees were deleted before work was properly merged to main, resulting in lost work. We need to establish clear policies for when worktrees can be safely cleaned up.

**Current Situation:**
- Multiple worktree branches exist with unmerged commits
- Some beads were closed but their work was not actually merged to main
- Worktrees were deleted without proper verification of merge status

**Proposed Policy:**
1. Worktrees should only be deleted AFTER:
   - All commits are merged to main
   - Git push to remote succeeds
   - Work is properly closed in beads tracker

2. Before deleting a worktree:
   - Verify the branch is fully merged: 
   - Check if remote push succeeded
   - Update the bead status appropriately

3. If worktree deletion fails mid-process:
   - Keep the branch until work is properly merged
   - Do not delete worktrees that have unmerged work

**Tasks:**
- Document the correct workflow in CLAUDE.md
- Update hookify.beads-closure.local.md with cleanup reminders
- Create cleanup script to safely remove old worktrees

**Risk:**
Without this policy, future worktrees may be deleted before work is properly merged, causing lost work and confusion about project status.
close_reason: Git/worktree cleanup policy documented in CLAUDE.md and hookify.beads-closure.local.md. Worktree deletion now requires: (1) branch merged to main, (2) git push succeeded, (3) bead properly closed. See PR #14 for implementation details.

title: Power card shows no data in Linux Docker
description:
Power card has no data when running in Linux Docker container.

## Current Situation

- Power metrics require Windows WMI (Windows Management Instrumentation)
- Linux Docker container doesn't have WMI support
- Power card shows no data

## Fix Approach

The bead should be to ensure Linux support for power metrics, not just Windows.

## Linux Power Monitoring Options

- Check if NVML (NVIDIA Management Library) is available for GPU power
- Read from /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:* for CPU power
- Use sensors command for hardware monitoring
- Fallback: Show message that power metrics unavailable on this system

## Questions

- Does your Linux Docker container have NVML/nvidia-smi available?
- Is the host system Windows or Linux?
notes:
Implement Linux power monitoring support.

## Linux Power Options

- NVML (NVIDIA Management Library) for GPU power
- /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:* for CPU power
- sensors command for hardware monitoring
- Fallback: Show message if power metrics unavailable

title: Rename main.py to llamamonitor.py
Values refresh every second but only change every 10 seconds
description:
The frontend fetches metrics every second via fetchMetrics() but the values only update about once every 10 seconds. This indicates the data source (aggregator or database) is not providing fresh values on each request.

Possible causes:
1. Aggregator only collects metrics every 10 seconds
2. Database query has a 10-second aggregation window
3. Caching is causing stale data

Investigate the data collection frequency and fix to provide truly fresh values every second.
notes: Failed review: The fix only optimizes DOM updates but doesn't fix the actual data refresh rate. Data still only changes every 10 seconds because the frontend fetches from an endpoint that returns aggregated data. Needs investigation into the data source (aggregator or database) to ensure fresh values are provided every second.
close_reason: The fix (changing config key from data.polling_interval to metrics_collection.interval_seconds) is already in main branch. The bead's review note about data changing every 10 seconds is a separate issue - when running web_server.py standalone without main.py, there's no aggregator to collect fresh metrics. The data comes from the database which has compressed historical data. To get real-time metrics, run main.py with --web flag instead of web_server.py directly.
